attributes.nuance_translation: A grammar point indicating that (A) is being received or obtained by the speaker, or another specified person.

attributes.body:
もらう is the 3rd verb that is regularly taught together with くれる, and あげる. It is used to highlight that (A) is 'received' by someone. However, unlike くれる and あげる (which are used to highlight that something is 'given'), もらう requires the に particle (or から) to mark the giver, not the recipient. が or は may be used to mark the recipient, as they are the one performing the action of receiving. を will mark the object that is being given.

In the second sentence we can see that the recipient has been omitted, while in the third example, the giver was omitted. This is a regular occurrence when using もらう, as the receiver is usually obvious, or the 'giver' may not be important to the overall meaning of the sentence.

In this example, the thing that was given is the focus, while the speaker does not consider the 'giver' something that needs to be mentioned. Sometimes, for very simple sentences with clear context, neither the 'giver', nor the 'receiver' needs to be mentioned.

attributes.description: Inner/outer circles and which verb to use
あげる, くれる, and もらう as Verbs

attributes.body: もらう is a basic verb meaning 'to receive,' often used when the speaker or someone in their in-group receives something from someone outside the group. For example, プレゼントをもらった means 'I received a present.' When used as てもらう after a verb in the て form, it shows that the speaker received the benefit of an action, as in 日本語を教えてもらった ('I had someone teach me Japanese').

first_relatable.title: もらう
first_relatable.meaning: To receive, To get, To obtain

second_relatable.title: てもらう
second_relatable.meaning: To get someone to do, To have someone do

attributes.body: あげる means 'to give' and is used when the speaker or someone in their in-group gives something to someone outside the group. The subject, marked by が, is the giver. In contrast, もらう means 'to receive' and describes the act from the receiver's perspective. With もらう, the subject marked by が is the one receiving.

first_relatable.title: もらう
first_relatable.meaning: To receive, To get, To obtain

second_relatable.title: あげる
second_relatable.meaning: To give (away), To present, To provide

attributes.body: くれる means 'to give' and is used when someone from the speaker's out-group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. The subject, marked with が, is the giver. In contrast, もらう means 'to receive' and describes the action from the receiver's perspective. With もらう, the subject marked with が is the one receiving.
